fact: TUNEPS director Sonia Ben Salem said 1,975 suppliers and 314 public buyers had already joined the TUNEPS online public procurement system.
Ben Salem said that from 1 September 2018 all ministries, non-administrative public enterprises and public establishments must conclude their public contracts through TUNEPS.
The OECD says TUNEPS runs e-bidding, e-contracting, e-catalogue and an e-shopping mall for tenders and small purchases.

The OECD says e-bidding covers the process from procurement plan to selection of the winning bid, e-contracting covers contract signature, and TUNEPS use has been mandatory for all contracting authorities since September 2019.
The OECD, citing TUNEPS, gives 2014-2019 totals of 1,032 registered public buyers, 7,037 suppliers, 3,350 procurement procedures and 6,400 e-shopping mall procedures.
The e-procurement platform TUNEPS is described by e-administration unit head Khaled Sellami as compulsory for any public purchase, with 1,300 public bodies and 12,000 suppliers on it.
Passage through TUNEPS is mandatory for every public purchase, according to the head of the e-administration unit.
TUNEPS is reported to have 1,300 public structures and 12,000 suppliers registered.
The president of the national public procurement observatory (HAICOP) reports that 1,536 public buyers and 17,835 suppliers were registered on the TUNEPS online purchasing system in 2024.
Government representatives told parliament's administration committee that the public procurement system is online, with more than 27,700 bids registered online and 15,500 suppliers and contractors.

Government representatives said the online public procurement system was adopted gradually from 2012 to 2014, tested, then made general and compulsory for all ministries and public institutions in 2019.
Government representatives gave a figure of more than 27,700 bids registered on the online public procurement system, with 15,500 suppliers and 1,441 public buyers registered.
